wstep: The Codex Alimentarius defines yogurt as milk fermented by symbiotic cultures of Streptococcus thermophilus and Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus.

ostrzezenia.tekst: FDA lists yogurt made from unpasteurized milk among high-risk foods.
Once the yogurt has set, keep it in the refrigerator at 40 °F (4.4 °C) or lower.

akapity: The sources used here do not describe a separate Bulgarian method, so this card follows the University of Illinois Extension basic yogurt recipe.
It does not give other temperatures, times or cultures, and it does not test any.
Illinois Extension uses 1 quart of 1% low-fat milk and 2 tablespoons of plain non-fat yogurt as the starter.
JarAtlas rule (cautious): make this yogurt only from pasteurized milk.
The starter must contain live bacteria, because cultures with dead bacteria will not make yogurt.
If you use purchased yogurt as the starter, use it before its “best by” or “sell by” date.
If you use a purchased yogurt culture, follow the manufacturer’s directions.
Heat the milk slowly to 180–185 °F (82–85 °C), stirring occasionally and checking the temperature with a thermometer.
Stir the starter into 1 cup of the warm milk until smooth, then pour it back into the pot and stir.
Pour the milk into containers with lids and incubate at 108–115 °F (42–46 °C) for 6–10 hours without moving them.
In the refrigerator the bacteria stop making more lactic acid, which is what makes yogurt more and more sour.
Incubating for too long makes the yogurt separate.
JarAtlas rule (cautious): do not make the yogurt more sour by incubating it for longer than 10 hours or by leaving it out of the refrigerator after it has set.
As soon as the yogurt has set, move it to the refrigerator at 40 °F (4.4 °C) or lower.
Illinois Extension says yogurt does not set when the starter had no live cultures, the incubation was too hot or too cold, or the equipment was not clean.
Fermented dairy products must reach a pH of 4.6 or less within 48 hours to be considered pathogen-free.
JarAtlas rule (cautious): if the yogurt has not set by the end of the incubation time, do not eat it.
